title: Stability Sentry: Mini-Cadence and Release Epilogue
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact field guide for a fast, safety-first release lane we are trialing for low-risk microfeatures and hotspot fixes. Focus: short watch windows, clear canary gates, operator playbook and a lightweight release epilogue template for capture and handoff.

Scope and goals:
- Ship small changes with < 1% user exposure during the mini-cadence window.
- Ensure telemetry coverage for latency, error-rate, and model-regression signals.
- Keep rollback decisions deterministic and quick (target: < 15 minutes decision + action).
- Produce a terse epilogue that surfaces immediate followups and owners within 2 business days.

Window & calendar (local times UTC):
- T-72h: branch cut and integration tests green (2027-11-02 10:00 UTC).
- T-24h: obs smoke run and canary config baked (2027-11-04 10:00 UTC).
- Release day (mini-window): 2027-11-05
  - 09:00 UTC: preflight standup (15m) — owners: A. Patel, M. Ruiz
  - 09:15 UTC: release push to canary (5% traffic)
  - 09:20–10:20 UTC: canary watch (1h) — rotating observer: SRE on-call
  - 10:20 UTC: canary decision checkpoint. If green, 50% ramp; if any gate trips, rollback to previous tag.
  - 10:30–11:30 UTC: ramp watch (1h) at 50%
  - 11:30 UTC: final ramp to 100% (if all gates pass)
  - 11:30–15:30 UTC: extended observation (4h) with hourly heartbeat posts to #release-watch

Preflight checklist (must be checked off before T-24h):
- [ ] PRs merged, changelog entry present and linked
- [ ] CI green for integration + smoke tests (include model inference smoke)
- [ ] Canary bucket / route configured and validated (traffic shaping tests ok)
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards for latency, p95/p99, error budget, model-quality-sanity exist and are pinned
- [ ] Synthetic probes set for representative customer flows (secrets scrubbed)
- [ ] Feature flag toggles created with safe default and kill switch
- [ ] Rollback playbook documented and practiced once inside staging run
- [ ] Pager rotations and on-call contacts published in release calendar

Canary gating criteria (pass/fail):
- Latency: no >15% increase in p95 compared to baseline for the 1h canary window
- Errors: API error-rate must not exceed baseline + 0.4% absolute or 3x baseline, whichever is lower
- Model regressions: automated eval set must not drop baseline quality by > 1.5% (metric: prompt-eval-accuracy)
- Resource signals: GPU memory pressure and host CPU should be within historical percentiles (no sustained > 85%)
- Business signal: key customer flows (two top customers) show no regression in success rate

Rollback matrix (decision ladder):
- Any critical production error or outage -> immediate rollback (target: 0–5m to trigger, 5–15m to complete)
- Canary metric breach (as defined above) -> pause ramp, investigate for 10m. If no mitigations, rollback at 15m
- Model-quality drift detected -> immediate rollback and run targeted evaluation job. Owner: Li. Chen
- Unidentified slow degradation with unknown root cause -> engage SRE and roll back within 15m

Operator quick-plays (for on-call):
- If alerts fire, post the first message to #release-watch with tag [mini-window-2027-11-05] and include: alert name, link, first 3 traces
- If rollback is needed: run rollback script (infra/scripts/rollback.sh) and confirm traffic restore in K8s ingress and LB within 5m
- If uncertainty: escalate to release commander (Aisha Patel) and open incident thread with template ID R-<date>-<seq>

Telemetry & observability checklist:
- Must-have dashboards: release-latency-over-time, release-errors-by-endpoint, model-eval-drift, feature-flag-usage
- Synthetic checks: confirm 3 synthetic flows succeeded in last 30m before canary
- Logging: ensure sampling for debug-level logs enabled for canary route only (do not enable globally)
- Traces: set temporary 100% trace-sampling for canary transactions for 1h window only

Communications brief (first 30 minutes):
- #release-watch: heartbeat posts at 0, 30, 60 minutes with short status (OK, investigating, rollback)
- Stakeholders: product and CSM pinged if canary passes 1h; immediate ping if rollback occurs
- External customers: Prepare pre-written note for impacted customers (templates in linked_artifacts)

Release epilogue template (to publish within 48h):
- Short summary: what shipped and why (2–3 lines)
- Release windows and timelines (as executed)
- Signals observed (latency, errors, user impacts) with graphs attached (links)
- Any immediate follow-ups and owners (L0 fixes and L1 investigations)
- Lessons learned and a short 'what we'd change next time' list
- Status: closed / ongoing / escalated with expected ETA

Draft release notes (to be copied into product-facing changelog):
- Feature: improved routing for low-latency prefix caching — reduces cold-start latency for mid-length prompts (~10–15% median improvement in internal tests).
- Fix: resolved a race condition in KV cache invalidation that could, in rare circumstances, return stale context to inference callers.
- Minor: adjusted autoscaler smoothing to reduce transient thrash during traffic bursts.

Known issues (callouts for customers):
- Edge-case: very long prompt sequences ( > 8k tokens) may still see higher p99 latency — workaround: use chunked prompts for now.
- Observability: a telemetry alert threshold was tightened in this release; we will re-baseline after 72h and may relax thresholds if noisy.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Are we comfortable with 1h canary for this class of change? Suggest running two test releases: one 1h, one 2h, compare signal stability.
- Follow-up: add a quick synthetic that exercises KV-invalidation scenario end-to-end. Owner: M. Ruiz.
- Consider automating the canary-decision with a short script that collects the four gating metrics and posts a summary to #release-watch.

Appendix: quick commands
- Check canary traffic: infra/scripts/canary-traffic-check --route=mini-window-2027-11-05
- Rollback: infra/scripts/rollback.sh --tag=previous-stable

End of doc.

(Notes: keep this doc as a living sketch; we'll convert parts to the runbook template if the mini-cadence repeats more than twice.)
